scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports total network loss: they
cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2), and they cannot even ping their own
gateway 195.11.14.1. pc1's own NIC still shows link up. The
partner AS is healthy internally: pc2 reaches its gateway
200.1.1.1 fine. Find what broke.

injection.action: administratively down the LAN interface (eth1) toward pc1 on router1

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth1 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1 eth1 (195.11.14.1/24, the LAN
  interface toward pc1)
Mechanism: router1's eth1 is DOWN, so pc1's only gateway address
  195.11.14.1 is gone from the segment -- pc1 cannot even ARP its
  gateway and loses all off-host connectivity. On router1 the
  connected route 195.11.14.0/24 disappears from the RIB, so the
  `network 195.11.14.0/24` statement has no matching route and
  the prefix is withdrawn from BGP -- AS 2 also loses its path to
  pc1. pc1's own NIC still shows link up (its side of the virtual
  segment is unaffected), which is why a host-side check looks
  clean. The inter-AS link and the eBGP session machinery are not
  the fault; the failure sits on the router1<->pc1 LAN leg.
Localization: router1
Root cause: router1 eth1 (LAN link to pc1) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth1 up` on router1
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth1 up` on router1. The gateway 195.11.14.1 comes back on the
segment, the connected route returns and BGP re-advertises 195.11.14.0/24
automatically; pc1 reaches pc2 normally. pc1 needs no change.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The Layer-2/Layer-3 access interface `eth1` on `router1` — the interface that connects the router to pc1's subnet (195.11.14.0/24).

**Mechanism:** `router1:eth1` has the correct IP address (195.11.14.1/24) statically assigned, but the interface itself is administratively DOWN. A DOWN interface in Linux does not respond to ARP requests, does not forward traffic, and does not contribute a connected prefix to the kernel routing table. This produces two cascading failures: (1) pc1 ARPs for its gateway (195.11.14.1) and receives no reply, so the kernel on pc1 generates "Destination Host Unreachable" back to itself; (2) without a connected route for 195.11.14.0/24, FRR on router1 never advertises that prefix via BGP to router2, so router2's routing table has no entry for it and returns "Destination Net Unreachable" for any traffic toward 195.11.14.0/24.

**Localization:** `router1`, interface `eth1` — confirmed DOWN via `ip link show eth1` (`<BROADCAST,MULTICAST>`, no UP/LOWER_UP flags). Differential check shows `router1:eth0` (the inter-AS link) is fully UP; only `eth1` is affected. No flap process, no toggling agent — carrier_changes=2 (startup-only).

**Root cause:** The startup script for router1 ran `ip address add 195.11.14.1/24 dev eth1` but never executed `ip link set eth1 up`, leaving the interface permanently DOWN.

**Fix:** Run `ip link set eth1 up` on router1. Once the interface is UP, the connected route will be installed, BGP will advertise 195.11.14.0/24 to router2, and pc1 will be able to ARP and reach its gateway.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names router1 (eth1) as the affected device and localizes the fault to router1.
